title: Inflight deserialization threadpool starvation and customer bridge
creator: Aditi Kapoor
description:
Summary:
A subset of Hosted API requests from heavy streaming customers hit a hot codepath that performs synchronous RPC deserialization on the main inference request handler threadpool. During tenant surge this caused worker starvation and cascading 5xx errors/timeouts, amplifying client retries. This issue primarily impacted long multipart and structured-output requests with embedded binary blobs and large function-call payloads.

Observed behavior:
- Sudden spike in 5xx/errors and streaming timeouts during two customer escalations on 2026-03-09 and 2026-03-10.
- Traces show request handlers spending 70-90% of processing time in protobuf deserialization and blob copy, blocking the bounded executor for request dispatch.
- Connection churn increased as client SDKs retried aggressively, which further increased queueing and kernel context-switch overhead.

Root cause hypothesis and confirmation:
- Root cause: synchronous CPU+alloc heavy deserialization performed inside the request dispatcher threadpool with no per-request size guard. Under tenant surge this exhausted the executor, causing head-of-line blocking and 5xx errors from the inference runtime when requests could not be scheduled.
- Confirmed by reproducing with synthetic multipart payloads in staging (see repro harness link below) and by flamegraphs showing high time in proto parsing.

Proposed fix and trade-offs:
- Short-term hotfix (urgent): move binary/protobuf deserialization to a dedicated bounded IO/parse executor (separate from inference dispatch pool) and add strict size limits and fast-fail behavior for oversized payloads. This reduces head-of-line blocking at the cost of additional copy/queue overhead.
- Medium-term: introduce adaptive admission that switches large-blob requests to an async streaming path with backpressure tokens and per-tenant concurrency limits.
- Rollout plan favors safety: canary on 10% of frontends in us-west-2 for 6 hours, then 33% then global if no regressions.

Runbook links and artifacts:
- Repro harness: https://confluence.redwood.ai/hosted/repro-deser-harness
- Grafana dashboard (staging & prod traces): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/9a3-deser/hosted-api-deser-flamegraphs
- PR (hotfix): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7432
- Postmortem draft: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1deser-incident-draft

Acceptance criteria:
- 99th percentile request latency reduced by >40% for deserialization-heavy workloads on canary hosts.
- No increase in overall CPU usage beyond expected parsing overhead across fleet.
- Canary shows no customer-visible 5xx surge; synthetic tests pass for edge cases (zero-length blobs, malformed proto, partial streaming frames).
